html:
Emir Abdelkader was a religious scholar and military leader who led the resistance to the French conquest of Algeria from 1832 to 1847. Algerians see him as the founder of their nation.

A Sufi from near Mascara, he was chosen as emir by the tribes of the west after the French invasion. He built a state with a capital, taxes, an army and arms factories, and made treaties with France. The French answered with scorched earth under General Bugeaud, burning crops and villages, and in 1847 he surrendered.

France broke its promise to let him go to the Middle East and held him for five years. He settled in Damascus, where in 1860 he sheltered thousands of Christians during the massacres. He was admired across Europe and America. See also Algeria.
